guides.title: Smartphone Battery Replacement & Charging Fix
safety_warnings: NEVER puncture or bend a lithium-ion battery — thermal runaway risk.
Power off the device completely before opening.
Do not use metal tools near the battery connector.
Work in a ventilated area away from flammables.
steps: Power off the phone completely and remove the SIM tray.
Apply a heated suction cup to the screen edge for 60 seconds to soften adhesive, then pull the screen up gently with the spudger.
Disconnect the battery flex cable connector using a plastic spudger — never metal.
Remove all screws securing the battery bracket, then carefully peel the battery using the pull-tab or a plastic tool.
Clean the battery bay with isopropyl alcohol on a cotton swab.
Place the new battery, reconnect the flex cable, reseat the screen, and test charge for 30 minutes before closing.

guides.title: Smartphone Screen & Digitizer Replacement
safety_warnings: Disconnect the battery before touching any flex cables.
Use only plastic tools near flex connectors to avoid short circuits.
Screen glass fragments are sharp — wear safety glasses.
steps: Power off the phone and disconnect the battery first.
Apply heat along the screen edges (60–80°C) to soften adhesive.
Insert the spudger at the bottom corner and carefully pry the screen assembly away from the frame.
Disconnect all display flex connectors (typically 2–3 ribbons).
Transfer any brackets or sensors from the old screen to the new assembly.
Reconnect flex cables, reconnect battery, test functionality before applying adhesive.
Apply fresh adhesive strips, press the screen firmly for 5 minutes.

guides.title: Smartphone Speaker / Microphone Repair
safety_warnings: Disconnect the battery before removing any internal components.
Avoid touching PCB components with bare hands — ESD risk.
steps: Power off and disconnect the battery.
Blast compressed air into the speaker grille — debris is the most common cause of muffled sound.
If no improvement, open the device and locate the speaker module.
Disconnect the speaker flex cable and remove the retaining bracket.
Swap in the replacement speaker, reconnect, and test before closing.

guides.title: Laptop Overheating — Thermal Paste & Fan Cleaning
safety_warnings: Shut down and unplug the laptop. Remove the battery if removable.
Ground yourself with an ESD wrist strap before touching the motherboard.
Allow the CPU/GPU to cool completely before applying thermal paste.
steps: Shut down, unplug, and remove the bottom panel screws.
Locate the fan and heatsink assembly. Use compressed air to blow dust from fins and fan blades.
Remove heatsink screws in a cross pattern (to avoid CPU die cracking), then lift the heatsink.
Clean old thermal paste from CPU/GPU die and heatsink contact plate using isopropyl alcohol and a lint-free cloth.
Apply a pea-sized dot of fresh thermal paste to the center of the CPU die.
Reseat the heatsink, tighten screws in a cross pattern, and reconnect the fan cable.
Boot the laptop and verify temperatures drop 10–20°C under load.

guides.title: Laptop Keyboard Key Repair / Replacement
safety_warnings: Power off and disconnect the charger before any keyboard work.
After a liquid spill, power off immediately and let dry for 48 hours minimum before attempting repair.
steps: For a single stuck key: use a plastic pry tool to gently pop off the keycap from one corner.
Clean under the key with a cotton swab and compressed air.
Inspect the scissor mechanism — realign or replace if broken.
Press the keycap back on until it clicks.
For full keyboard replacement: remove the bottom panel, disconnect the keyboard ribbon cable, unscrew the keyboard, and swap in the replacement.

guides.title: Laptop No Power / Won't Boot Diagnosis
safety_warnings: Do not open the laptop while connected to mains power.
Check for swollen or leaking batteries before handling.
steps: Test with a known-good charger. Measure charger DC output with a multimeter — should match laptop spec (e.g., 19V).
Remove the battery and try powering on with only the charger — rules out dead battery.
Perform a hard reset: hold power button for 30 seconds with battery removed and charger unplugged.
Reseat RAM sticks — remove them, clean contacts with an eraser, reinsert firmly.
If still no power, test the DC power jack for continuity and check for bent pins.

guides.title: Headphone Cable Fault — Repair or Replacement
safety_warnings: Work in a ventilated area when soldering — flux fumes are irritating.
Do not overheat the driver housing — sustained heat damages the membrane.
steps: Flex the cable near the plug and near each ear cup while playing audio — if sound cuts in/out, you've found the fault zone.
Cut the cable 2cm either side of the fault. Strip and tin the exposed wires.
Match wire colours: typically Red = Right, Blue/Green = Left, Copper/Bare = Ground.
Twist matching wires together, solder, and cover each joint individually with heat shrink.
Test continuity with a multimeter across the repaired section before final assembly.
If the 3.5mm plug is faulty, cut it off, thread new heat shrink onto the cable, solder to a replacement TRS plug: Tip = Left, Ring = Right, Sleeve = Ground.

guides.title: Headphone Ear Pad Replacement
safety_warnings: Do not use sharp tools near the driver mesh — puncturing it will damage the speaker.
steps: Rotate or peel the old ear pad counterclockwise (most snap-on pads) or pull it straight off.
Clean the mounting ring with a damp cloth and allow to dry.
Align the new ear pad with the mounting ring and press firmly around the circumference until it snaps into place.
Test fit by pressing the headphone to your ear — no gaps should be present.

guides.title: Headphone Headband Crack Repair
safety_warnings: Ensure epoxy is fully cured (24h) before flexing the headband.
steps: Clean the crack surfaces with isopropyl alcohol and lightly sand for better adhesion.
Mix epoxy per instructions and apply to both surfaces.
Press together firmly and clamp or tape in alignment.
Allow 24 hours full cure before use.
For structural cracks, reinforce with a strip of self-fusing silicone tape over the joint.

guides.title: Tablet Battery Replacement
safety_warnings: NEVER use metal tools to pry a lithium-ion battery — puncture causes fire.
If the battery is visibly swollen, do not charge it. Place the device in a fireproof container.
Power off completely before opening.
steps: Power off the tablet and heat the edges with a heat gun at low setting (60°C) to soften adhesive.
Use a suction cup to create separation, then run a spudger along all four edges.
Locate and disconnect the battery flex cable before touching anything else.
Peel the battery using the pull tab or plastic lever — never metal.
Clean the bay with isopropyl alcohol, install the new battery, reconnect the cable.
Test power on before resealing. Apply new adhesive strips and press the back cover for 5 minutes.

guides.title: Tablet Touchscreen Digitizer Replacement
safety_warnings: Disconnect the battery before removing display connectors.
Wear safety glasses — cracked glass can shed sharp fragments.
steps: Power off and disconnect the battery.
Heat the screen perimeter at 60–80°C for 2 minutes to soften adhesive.
Apply suction cup to the top of the screen, pull to create a gap, insert spudger.
Slowly trace the spudger around all four edges to release adhesive.
Disconnect all digitizer and display flex cables.
Clean the frame of old adhesive. Install new adhesive strips.
Connect the new digitizer, test touch function before sealing, then press closed.

guides.title: Tablet Charging Port Repair
safety_warnings: Disconnect the battery before any soldering work.
Work in a ventilated area. Do not overheat the PCB — sustained heat causes trace lift.
steps: Open the tablet and disconnect the battery.
Locate the charging port — on most tablets it is a flex-mounted module.
If flex-mounted: disconnect the ribbon cable, unscrew, and swap in the new module.
If soldered directly to PCB: apply flux, use solder wick to remove old solder, heat each pin with iron, lift the old port, clean pads.
Align the new port over the pads, tack two corner pins first, then solder all pins.
Inspect joints under magnification. No bridges. Test charge before reassembly.

guides.title: Wired Earbud — Single-Side Audio Fix
safety_warnings: Work in a ventilated area when soldering.
The driver housing is very small — do not apply heat for more than 3 seconds at a time.
steps: Flex the cable near the jack and near the silent earbud while playing audio to find the break point.
Cut and strip wire at the fault. Match colour coding: Right = Red, Left = Blue/Green, Ground = Copper.
Twist, solder, and individually insulate each wire with heat shrink.
Test audio continuity with a multimeter before sealing.
If driver itself is silent after cable check, open the earbud housing and resolder the hair-thin driver wires.

guides.title: Earbud Silicone Tip Replacement
tools_needed: Replacement silicone tips (S/M/L matching stem diameter)
safety_warnings: Ensure tips fully seat on the nozzle — a loose tip can become lodged in the ear canal.
steps: Pinch and pull the old tip straight off the nozzle.
Inspect the nozzle mesh for wax buildup — clean with a dry toothbrush.
Stretch the new tip over the nozzle and press firmly until the inner groove snaps into place.
Tug gently to confirm it is secure before use.

guides.title: TWS Earbud — Pairing Reset & Charging Case Fix
safety_warnings: Do not immerse the case in liquid — moisture damage will void repair options.
steps: Factory reset: place both earbuds in the case, hold the case button for 10+ seconds until LEDs flash reset pattern (refer to model manual).
Delete the device from your phone Bluetooth list, then re-pair from scratch.
If case won't charge: clean the case charging pins with a dry cotton swab and isopropyl alcohol.
Clean the earbud contact pads inside the case with a dry toothpick — oxidation buildup is the most common cause of poor charging.

guides.title: Smartwatch Battery Replacement
safety_warnings: Smartwatch batteries are extremely small — puncture risk is high. Use only plastic tools.
Power off completely before opening.
Do not attempt if battery is swollen — place in a fireproof bag.
steps: Power off the watch and remove any bands.
Heat the back cover at 50–60°C to loosen adhesive. Apply suction cup and gently pry the back.
Disconnect the battery flex cable connector using a plastic spudger.
Remove the battery using the pull tab — never lever with metal.
Fit the replacement battery, reconnect the flex cable, test power on.
Apply new adhesive gasket or UV adhesive around the perimeter and press the back cover closed for 2 minutes.

guides.title: Smartwatch Digital Crown / Button Fix
safety_warnings: Do not spray isopropyl alcohol directly into crown gap — use a cotton swab.
steps: Turn the crown rapidly 20+ times to work out debris — often resolves stiffness.
Apply a tiny amount of isopropyl alcohol around the crown gap with a cotton swab, then rotate to distribute.
Blast the crown gap with compressed air.
If still stuck: open the case, remove the crown assembly, clean the seal and O-ring, reinstall.

guides.title: Smartwatch Screen Glass Replacement
safety_warnings: Cracked smartwatch glass is extremely sharp — wear gloves and safety glasses.
Disconnect the battery before removing the display assembly.
steps: Power off. Heat the screen at 60°C for 90 seconds.
Apply suction cup and pull while running spudger around the perimeter.
If only the glass is cracked (OLED intact), use UV adhesive to bond replacement glass.
If OLED is damaged, disconnect the battery, then disconnect the display flex cable and swap the full assembly.
Apply UV adhesive around the frame, seat the new screen, cure under UV lamp for 60 seconds.
